My strategy for testing code typically involves writing comprehensive unit tests for each component or function to ensure they perform as expected under various conditions. For instance, in my Scala-based projects like the Tic-Tac-Toe game, I use munit.FunSuite to define tests that cover all possible game scenarios, such as checking for complete rows or handling different win conditions, as seen in `shared/src/test/scala/TicTacToeTests.scala`. In TypeScript projects, I use vitest, as shown in src/index.test.ts for the DarkModeToggle component. The tests cover functionality like initializing based on system preference and toggling themes on click, ensuring both the logic and UI elements behave correctly. These tests ensure robustness in code and allow me to ref actor with confidence, knowing that breaking changes will be caught quickly.
